clue.text: Girl in West Side Story fails to start song

indicators.note: something that fails to start is missing its opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of the musical West Side Story

explanation.surface: A singer playing the heroine of a musical misses her cue as the number begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to start' removes M from MARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or similar work.

clue.text: Give evidence during trial

parts.note: at can mean during, as in 'at night'
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A witness testifies in the course of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during trial' reads as one courtroom phrase, but each word does its own job; 'during' gives the short word for at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or declare something true, as one does in testimony.

clue.text: Boss, hard-working, having debts cancelled

indicators.note: debts that are cancelled are struck out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: studious means diligent at study, hard-working
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A diligent employer gets their debts written off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but it is the raised knob sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is an ornamental knob or boss projecting from a surface.

clue.text: Gamble taking breather during exercise

indicators.note: placed during the exercise means set inside its letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a lung is the organ one breathes with

explanation.surface: Someone takes a rest in the middle of a workout and has a flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest, but it is a lung.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to bet or spend recklessly, a big gamble.

clue.text: Worker needing fine body parts

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an arm and a hand are both parts of the body

explanation.surface: A labourer is wanted who is in good physical shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhand is a labourer employed on a farm.

clue.text: A warm spell centrally then storms — he might say that

indicators.note: storms suggests letters thrown into turmoil and rearranged
taking a word centrally means using only its middle letter

explanation.surface: A forecast: a warm spell in the middle of the week, then storms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' takes E, the middle letter of 'spell'; 'storms' rearranges A WARM, E and THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecaster on television would deliver exactly this kind of outlook for the coming week.

clue.text: Mostly grumpy character in bar

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: crotchety means irritable, grumpy

explanation.surface: An irritable regular is propping up the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is not a pub but a bar of music, and the 'character' is a note in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note of one beat, written in a bar of music.

clue.text: Makes great effort to pick up name that's surprising!

indicators.note: the first word picks up the second by taking it inside itself

parts.note: heaves means strains or pulls hard

explanation.surface: Someone straining to lift a name is amazed by it.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Heavens!' is an exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Drunk prepared to be fired

definitions.meaning: said of a gun with ammunition in it

explanation.surface: An inebriated employee is about to lose their job.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for intoxicated and also describes a gun charged with ammunition.

clue.text: Arrived with artist one means to produce portrait

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter turns up with a way of making a likeness.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer's apparatus is one way to produce a portrait.

clue.text: Explosive made tiny fragments

indicators.note: fragments is a verb here: breaks the letters apart to be reassembled

explanation.surface: A blast blew something into tiny pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fragments' looks like a noun, but it is a verb signalling the anagram of MADE TINY.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a high explosive, invented by Alfred Nobel.

clue.text: Outwit in front of girlfriend? Things go off after that

parts.note: to best someone is to outwit them
before means in front of
a date can be the person one is going out with

explanation.surface: Someone tries to impress a girlfriend; things go wrong afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' looks like a row or falling-out, but it means food spoiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Food labelled with this day is past its prime afterwards: it spoils, or goes off.

clue.text: Strangely, men bet not to cover mass burial

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover by going round the other piece
strangely means the letters come out in an odd new order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Oddly, the men refuse a wager on a mass burial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges MEN BET NOT, and 'to cover' wraps those letters around M.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing a body in a tomb is a form of burial.

clue.text: The last one to appear in home game

indicators.note: the answer appears inside these words, concealed across the gap

explanation.surface: The final player takes the field in a fixture at the home ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the last of anything.

clue.text: Get topless to make an impression

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: to fetch is to go and get

explanation.surface: Going topless is a way of getting noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' simply means drop the first letter of FETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design, cutting an impression into a surface.

clue.text: Watering device you once put in place to encourage plant growth

indicators.note: put in means the second piece is set inside the first

parts.note: a hose waters a garden
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A gardener installs a watering hose to help plants grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated greenhouse is used to bring on plants quickly.

clue.text: Partner's issue on leaving flight

indicators.note: with the word on leaving, those letters are taken away

parts.note: a spouse's son from an earlier relationship is a stepson

explanation.surface: A couple's child is about to board a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like a plane journey, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a series of stairs, a set of steps.

clue.text: Miss a captain

parts.note: to skip is to miss out
per means a or each, as in 'ten pounds per head'

explanation.surface: A young woman is a ship's commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a woman's title, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the master of a ship or leader of a team.

clue.text: Obscure European coin

parts.note: dim means faint or obscure

explanation.surface: A rare continental coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is a US ten-cent coin.

clue.text: Developing match stamina, i.e. they work out a lot

indicators.note: developing means taking new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Athletes building up endurance for a match train hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' looks like gym training, but it means calculate.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematicians spend their time calculating and solving problems.

clue.text: Current navigator's device needs to start

indicators.note: needs here means lacks, so the word lacks its first letter

parts.note: a sextant measures angles for navigation

explanation.surface: A navigator's instrument needs to be got going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' means 'lacks', so 'needs to start' drops S.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still existing, current.

clue.text: Mean nurse to support home

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes beneath the other

parts.note: in means at home
to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: A spiteful nurse is about to look after someone at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to mean to do it.

clue.text: Fake the compiler's advertisement

parts.note: the setter says 'I am', shortened to I'm
a poster is a printed advertisement

explanation.surface: The setter's notice is a phoney.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposter is someone pretending to be another, a fake.

clue.text: Shrub sprang up

definitions.meaning: the past tense of a verb meaning ascend

explanation.surface: A bush suddenly grew tall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a thorny flowering shrub and also the past tense meaning got up.

clue.text: It arouses pity giving power to musketeer

parts.note: Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers

explanation.surface: Something touching makes a swordsman stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or life that evokes sadness or pity.

clue.text: Old soldiers warning

parts.note: men means soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Veterans issue a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of things to come, often a warning.

clue.text: Harmony is found in rejection of what's unacceptable

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the other piece
rejection, a throwing back, means the word is turned round

parts.note: non-U is British slang for not upper-class, socially unacceptable
taken as written

explanation.surface: Peace is achieved by turning down what offends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' gives UNON; 'found in' places the clue's 'is' inside. U and non-U were 1950s British labels for upper-class and not upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in harmony, together.

clue.text: Group of horses leading lady for hack

parts.note: a string is the horses trained at one stable
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, the country's leading lady

explanation.surface: A stable's horses follow the lead of a woman on a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' could be a riding horse in this horsey surface, but it is a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringer is a freelance journalist paid per piece, a hack.
